semanticDecisions: the signal is still conservative: a block passes a unit only when both of the unit's bits are set, and every unit of the block sets its two bits, so no occurrence is ever missed; a false pass costs the exact-mask lookup, as before

the bits are unfolded: the whole-String facts fold A..Z onto a..z so that case-insensitive gates can share them, which costs the position index selectivity for nothing; the walks are exact; confining a unit's two bits to one word partitions the alphabet over four 63-bit filters, which rejects more than one 255-bit filter would

four words per block cost 32 bytes per 64 units, 0.5 bytes per unit, against the 8 bytes per 64 units before; the retained-bytes ceiling grows accordingly and the invariant-6 guard test pins the new figure

every word of a published signal carries bit 0, so each word stands on its own and a block test reads exactly one word, as the 64-bit signal did; two threads publishing the same block write identical words
the A37/A38 hand-off rule stays as the guard for alphabets dense enough to pass through 255 bits too; with the wider signal it fires far less often
